title: & and | used where a short-circuit guard was intended
purpose: Prevent a NOMETHOD/NOSTRING crash on the right-hand operand when the left-hand operand alone would have made evaluating the right-hand one unnecessary and unsafe.
trigger: A `&` or `|` expression combines two conditions where the right-hand condition would raise a condition (most commonly a NOMETHOD error from indexing or negating .nil) if evaluated in isolation, and the left-hand condition exists specifically to guard against that case. ooRexx's `&` and `|` operators always evaluate both operands; they are not short-circuiting the way `and`/`or` are in Python or `&&`/`||` are in C-family languages.
evidence_note: This project's own Alchemy conventions already record it: '& does not short-circuit -- use nested if'. It was also the confirmed root cause of a real crash traced this session in an unrelated component: a predicate `if \\left["ok"] | \\right["ok"] then return .nil` failed with 'The NIL object does not understand message "\\"' because a prior evaluation step could leave left["ok"] genuinely unset (.nil) rather than an explicit boolean, and `\\` applied to .nil is itself a NOMETHOD error, independent of the missing short-circuit.
correct: Replace `if guard & risky then ...` with nested guards: `if guard then do; if risky then ...; end`. Where the risky operand cannot itself be .nil-safe, check it explicitly (`x \\== .nil`) rather than relying on evaluation order that ooRexx does not provide.
compiler_relationship: Both operands are always evaluated by design; this is documented ooRexx operator semantics, not a translator bug. The rule is about a common incorrect assumption carried over from short-circuiting languages, not about non-conformant code.
return_semantics: A LanguageRulePage may be opened and then return to the originating cycle selector.
